target.note_url: same Worker as api.betterflag.app, same Better Stack source

methodology.generator: tools/loadtest/api-loadtest.mjs (open-loop, fixed cadence, not gated on responses)
methodology.stages_run_separately: each stage ran in its own process because the sandbox suspends background processes between calls

server_latency_source.meaning: the Worker's own span duration (auth + KV snapshot read + evaluate). Excludes network RTT. EDGE_LOG_SUCCESS_SAMPLE_RATE = 1, so every request is logged.

methodology.client_latency_meaning: round-trip time observed from the load generator. Includes network distance to the nearest Cloudflare PoP, so it is NOT a measure of the edge itself.

headline.verdict: P50/P95 flat across an 8x load increase (25 -> 200 RPS). No degradation, no errors.

cost.note: all-flags mode bills one evaluation per flag returned, so 8 per request

findings: Server-side P50 is 6-7ms and P95 is 8-10ms, essentially flat from 25 to 200 RPS. The worker is not the bottleneck at this load.
P99 stays in single/low double digits until 200 RPS, where it rises to 23ms. Still far inside the <50ms product claim.
Only 36 of 11,254 requests (0.32%) exceeded 50ms. The 312/488ms maxima are isolated cold-start / isolate spin-up outliers, not sustained degradation.
Zero non-200 responses across the whole ramp.
The hot-path budget in apps/api/src/index.ts says 'p50 < 10ms'. Measured P50 = 7ms, inside budget.
Client-observed RTT (~25-29ms p50) is dominated by network distance from the generator, which is why the Better Stack duration_ms figure is the one to quote.
caveats: 200 RPS is the ceiling actually tested; it is not a breaking-point test. The worker showed no strain, so the real limit is higher and untested.
Load originated from a single host in one region, so this does not exercise multi-PoP behaviour.
The evaluated project is a KV-only bench fixture (bench-e2e-flag-0..7), not a database-backed project.
